name: The Restricted Section of Soft Shields

exhibits.title: The Four Monographs
exhibits.text: Four bound volumes on a single shelf of the Restricted Section, each explaining the same mystery: why the projector head — the funnel between encoder and loss — shields the encoder, and why we cut it off when training ends. One cover bears a lattice of dots (SimCLR, the first sighting); one is titled in grim gilt (Guillotine Regularization); one is slim and dense with gradients (Xue et al.); the last is stamped with an hourglass narrow at the middle (the Information Bottleneck). Four covens, four framings, one phenomenon: the head does the work of being wrong, so the body may do the work of being right.

exhibits.title: The Guillotine: Snip the Head, the Body Sings On
exhibits.text: SimCLR (Chen et al., ICML 2020) first noticed, almost by accident, that discarding the projector head after training made the encoder perform BETTER on tasks it was never trained for — observation, not yet mathematics. Guillotine Regularization (Bordes et al., NeurIPS 2023) named the practice and measured it: severing the projector can raise downstream performance by more than thirty percentage points. Their framing: the head overfits to the PRETEXT task, and when pretext and downstream are misaligned that overfitting is harmful — but LOCALIZED in the head. The encoder is spared because the head takes the blow.

exhibits.title: Where the Strain Settles
exhibits.text: Why does the strain settle in the upper layers and not the lower? Xue and her collaborators (ICLR 2024) traced the gradients themselves: the implicit bias of gradient-based training causes pretext-useful features to migrate, slowly and inexorably, TOWARD the funnel's output, while features useful for downstream tasks settle into the encoder. The non-linearities in the funnel make this functional specialization possible. It is not architecturally enforced — it is EMERGENT, a consequence of how gradients flow through non-linear layers during long training.

exhibits.title: A Soft Buffer, Not a Hard Guard
exhibits.text: The Information Bottleneck monograph (ICLR 2025) gives the shield its information-theoretic spine: the funnel is secretly a bottleneck. It compresses out information irrelevant to the self-supervised objective, and because the encoder lies UPSTREAM of the compression, the encoder retains the broader signal; the funnel's own parameters absorb the optimization burden and attenuate the gradient reaching the encoder. But the protection is imperfect — gradients still flow through, and strong augmentations or excessively long training can bleed distortion into the body. The thickness of the shield is set by the funnel's depth, its non-linearities, and the alignment between augmentation and downstream use.

exhibits.title: The Shield in Cross-Section
exhibits.caption: The projector head absorbs the pretext task's distortion; the encoder representation upstream of it is what survives the guillotine and serves downstream tasks.

exhibits.title: Madam Quillright
exhibits.subtitle: Librarian of the Restricted Section
exhibits.text: It is a soft buffer, not a hard guard — do write that down. Gradients still flow through the funnel into the encoder beneath; the funnel merely redistributes the pressure. The singer is shielded not behind a wall, but behind a body that absorbs and releases the worst of the blow. Four covens have written on this — observation from SimCLR, the thirty-point leap of the Guillotine manuscript, Xue's tracing of the migrating gradients, and the bottleneck framing — and a student of the predictive arts should be able to recite all four. As one of my Slytherins once put it, inelegantly but correctly: we discard the head after training because the head has done the work of being wrong, and the body has done the work of being right.

exhibits.title: Chapter 3: The Soft Shield of the Projector
exhibits.text:
It was in the third week of term that the librarian, Madam Quillright, took a small group of older students into the Restricted Section to read a quartet of bound monographs that had been arriving at Hogwarts, one at a time, over the past several years. "You have seen the Expander in the Charms corridor," she said. "What you have not yet been told is *why* it works — and on this question, four schools of magical philosophy have each written something worth hearing."

She lifted down the first volume, its cover stamped with a simple lattice of dots. "The earliest sighting was recorded by the SimCLR coven [[ref:chen2020]]. They observed, almost by accident, that when they discarded the funnel after training and tested only the singer's voice on tasks she had never been trained for, she sang *better* than when the funnel was still attached. They proposed an explanation — that the funnel absorbed the strain of pretending two glimpses of the same thing were identical, and so the singer was spared from having to discard the small differences between augmentations. But they offered no mathematics of the gradient. Only observation."

She set it aside and lifted a second volume, bound in a darker leather and titled in gilt. "The Guillotine Regularization manuscript [[ref:bordes2023]] gave the practice its grim name. Snip off the head, they said, and the body sings on. They reported that severing the funnel could raise the singer's performance on certain downstream rituals by more than thirty percentage points — a leap so dramatic that the wizarding journals refused to print it for some months. Their framing was this: the funnel overfits to the *pretext task*, the task used during training. When the pretext task and the downstream task are misaligned, the overfitting is harmful — but, crucially, it is *localized* to the funnel. The encoder is spared because the funnel takes the blow."

A Slytherin girl, eyes narrowed, asked: "But why does the funnel take the blow and not the encoder? What makes the strain settle in the upper layers rather than the lower?"

"That," said Madam Quillright, "is the question the third manuscript answers most precisely." She lifted a slim, mathematically dense volume. "Xue and her collaborators [[ref:xue2024]] traced the gradients themselves. They showed that the implicit bias of gradient-based training causes pretext-useful features to migrate, slowly and inexorably, *toward* the funnel's output — while features useful for downstream tasks settle into the encoder. The non-linearities in the funnel make this functional specialization possible. It is not architecturally enforced. It is *emergent* — a consequence of how gradients flow through non-linear layers during long training."

She lifted the fourth and final volume, its cover stamped with a small hourglass narrow at the middle. "And the most recent — the Information Bottleneck monograph [[ref:projhead2025]] — gave the phenomenon an information-theoretic spine. The funnel, they argued, is secretly a bottleneck. It compresses out information irrelevant to the self-supervised objective, and because the encoder lies *upstream* of this compression, the encoder retains the broader signal. The funnel's own parameters absorb the optimization burden, attenuating the gradient signal that ever reaches the encoder."

Madam Quillright closed the four volumes and set them in a line on the reading desk. "So you see, four covens, four framings, one phenomenon. The encoder is not perfectly protected — strong augmentations or excessively long training can still bleed through. But the funnel concentrates the distortion of the pretext task within itself. The depth of the funnel, the non-linearities within it, and the alignment between augmentation and downstream use — these together determine how thick the shield is."

She looked up at the students. "It is a *soft buffer, not a hard guard*. Gradients still flow through the funnel into the encoder beneath. But the funnel redistributes the pressure. The singer is shielded — not behind a wall, but behind a body that absorbs and releases the worst of the blow."

The Slytherin girl nodded slowly. "So we discard the head after training because the head has done the work of being wrong, and the body has done the work of being right."

"Inelegantly put," said Madam Quillright, "but yes."

exhibits.title: The soft shield in three views: guillotine, migration, bottleneck
exhibits.caption: Three framings of why we cut off the projector head when training ends, and why the body sings on without it. (a) The Guillotine: across self-supervised setups, evaluating on the encoder's representation after REMOVING the head outperforms evaluating on the head's projection — a gain that can exceed thirty points (Bordes et al., NeurIPS 2023). It is the characteristic pattern, not a single benchmark. (b) Gradient feature migration: the implicit bias of gradient training sorts features by usefulness across the non-linear funnel — pretext-task-useful features drift toward the head's OUTPUT, while broadly-useful downstream features settle in the ENCODER. The specialization is emergent, not architecturally enforced (Xue et al., ICLR 2024). (c) Information bottleneck: the head is secretly a bottleneck that compresses out information irrelevant to the SSL objective and absorbs the optimization burden, attenuating the gradient that reaches the encoder; because the encoder sits UPSTREAM of the compression, it keeps the broader signal (ICLR 2025). One phenomenon, three lenses: the head does the work of being wrong so the body may do the work of being right.
